 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Weather Weather PAGASA: 12 areas to experience drought in November amid El Niño 
 By MARIEL CELINE SERQUIÑA , GMA News Published October 22, 2026 4:24pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Twelve areas in the Philippines are forecast to experience drought in November 2026 as a strong El Niño is expected to persist until the first quarter of 2027, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
 Based on PAGASA's climate outlook for November 2026 to April 2027, the following areas are expected to experience drought in November:
 Albay
 Camarines Norte
 Camarines Sur
 Catanduanes
 Capiz
 Leyte
 Negros Oriental
 Western Samar
 Siquijor
 Southern Leyte
 City of Isabela
 Misamis Oriental
 PAGASA defines drought as three consecutive months of way-below-normal rainfall, or a reduction of more than 60% from the average, or five consecutive months of below-normal rainfall, or a reduction of 21% to 60% from the average.
 Meanwhile, the following areas are forecast to experience dry spells in November:

 Luzon: Abra, Apayao, Bataan, Batanes, Batangas, Benguet, Cagayan, Cavite, Ifugao, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Isabela, Kalinga, La Union, Marinduque, Masbate, Metro Manila, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Palawan, Pangasinan, Quezon, Quirino, Romblon, Sorsogon and Zambales.
 Visayas: Aklan, Antique, Biliran, Bohol, Cebu, Guimaras, Iloilo, Negros Occidental and Northern Samar.
 Mindanao: Basilan, Camiguin, Cotabato (North Cotabato), Davao del Sur, Davao Occidental, Dinagat Islands, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Misamis Occidental, Sarangani, South Cotabato, Special Geographic Area (SGA), Sultan Kudarat, Sulu, Surigao del Norte, Tawi-Tawi, Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga del Sur and Zamboanga Sibugay.
 PAGASA defines a dry spell as three consecutive months of below-normal rainfall, or a reduction of 21% to 60% from the average, or two consecutive months of way-below-normal rainfall, or a reduction of more than 60% from the average.
 The following areas, meanwhile, are expected to experience dry conditions in November:
 Aurora
 Bulacan
 Laguna
 Nueva Ecija
 Pampanga
 Rizal
 Tarlac
 Eastern Samar
 Agusan del Sur
 Davao Oriental
 Surigao del Sur
 PAGASA defines a dry condition as two consecutive months of below-normal rainfall, or a reduction of 21% to 60% from the average.
 At a media briefing in Makati City on Thursday, PAGASA Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section chief Ana Liza Solis said most areas in the Visayas and Mindanao were expected to experience prolonged dry spells or drought.
 “While we will be experiencing the onset of the rainy season next year during the Southwest Monsoon, those areas situated along the western section [are expected to see relief from the] dry spell and drought,” Solis said.
 “Those areas along the Visayas and Mindanao will still be experiencing prolonged dry spell or drought,” she added.
 PAGASA earlier said the average temperature across the Philippines could rise by 1 to 2 degrees Celsius during El Niño.
 Several government agencies have also rolled out initiatives, developed plans and introduced technologies to mitigate the effects of extreme heat and prolonged dry conditions.
 The public has been advised to start storing and conserving water amid the possibility of supply shortages as drought conditions worsen. — VBL, GMA News
